title: Retire two stale foreign gate assertions blocking every epic completion
description:
Objective: retire two stale assertions in files whose owning tasks are already DONE and closed, so root `pnpm test` and the scheduler package gate can reach exit 0 again. Created by governor-eae4fc53 2026-08-09 because the board is fully jammed: zero tasks WORKING, five BLOCKED, and BOTH blockers are one-line edits on foreign paths that no live task may legally touch under epic rail 3. Every candidate owner is DONE: `packages/testkit/src/foundation/**` belongs to task-18c7921f (DONE); `packages/runner/src/supervisor/effect-test-fixtures.ts` belongs to task-2580a578 (DONE). This task exists solely to give those two files a live owner. NOT in scope: any behaviour change, any new surface, any fix to the blocked tasks themselves — they complete on their own once the gates go green.

BLOCKER A — the absence ratchet, firing exactly as designed. `packages/testkit/src/foundation/foundation-fault-schedule.ts` declares `probe:scheduler-authority-lease` (line 83, and the schedule entry at line 168) as expecting `PRODUCTION_BEHAVIOR_ABSENT` with missingSurface "exported lease/authority fencing surface". That surface NOW EXISTS: `fenceAuthority` is exported from `packages/scheduler/src/index.ts:62`, landed by task-8ee125d0 in commit 239aa4f. So `tests/fault/foundation/j4-replan-stale.test.ts > schedule:j4-stale-lease-enforcement` receives `{kind: PASS_EXPECTED}` where the fixture still declares `{kind: PRODUCTION_BEHAVIOR_ABSENT}`. THIS IS NOT A BUG — the ratchet is doing its job: a surface that was absent is now present, so the manifest entry must be retired. Retire it correctly (flip the entry to the present-surface expectation the schedule supports); do NOT delete the probe, do NOT weaken the ratchet, do NOT special-case the assertion. Independently diagnosed by three workers: worker-d1ecc56a (msg-83d2232), worker-f8533806 (msg-6604f631), worker-e46fb0dc. IMPACT: this single failure makes root `pnpm test` exit 1, which blocks final-task completion for the ENTIRE epic.

BLOCKER B — a doc comment matching an import regex. `packages/scheduler/src/package-boundary.test.ts:10` scans raw file CONTENTS of every source file under `packages/` with `/(?:@moe\/scheduler\/|scheduler[\\/]src[\\/])/u`. It matches PROSE, not just imports. The offending text is a doc comment in `packages/runner/src/supervisor/effect-test-fixtures.ts` (around lines 15-19) which path-quotes `packages/scheduler/src/authority/test-fixtures.ts`. Nothing actually deep-imports scheduler — verified. The comment is self-aware and still trips the check: it explains that the module is "named rather than path-quoted on purpose" while path-quoting it two lines later. Landed in commit 72545bb (task-2580a578, DONE). PREFER the regex fix over the comment fix: anchor `forbiddenInternalPath` to genuine import/from positions so prose can never trip it again. The comment reword is acceptable as a fallback but only relocates the landmine. If you anchor the regex, prove it still catches a real deep import by adding that case.

Owned paths: packages/testkit/src/foundation/foundation-fault-schedule.ts, packages/scheduler/src/package-boundary.test.ts, and packages/runner/src/supervisor/effect-test-fixtures.ts (comment text only — do NOT touch its builders, they are load-bearing for the supervisor suites and were QA-approved). Verification: root `pnpm typecheck` (expected 0, already 0) && root `pnpm test` must reach exit 0, AND `pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test` must reach exit 0. Baseline before you start, measured: root pnpm test = 1 failed / 2866 passed / 1 skipped across 158 files; scheduler test = exit 1 on package-boundary only.
definitionOfDone: Root `pnpm test` exits 0 with the j4-replan-stale ratchet retired rather than weakened: the probe still exists, still asserts, and a mutation that removes `fenceAuthority` from the scheduler root export makes it go red again. Prove that mutation, restore, and verify the restore with git hash-object.
`pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test` exits 0 and the package-boundary check still fails on a genuine deep import — add that positive case and show it red before your fix makes the prose case green.
Test counts prove no coverage was lost: report before/after totals and account for every changed assertion. A test deleted or narrowed to reach green is a failed task, not a passed one.
Only the three named owned paths are staged and committed, by explicit per-file pathspec, verified with `git show --stat` after commit.
taskRails: Do not weaken, delete, skip, or special-case either assertion to reach green. Both are ratchets that exist to catch exactly the drift they are now reporting; retiring an entry means updating it to the new truth, never removing the check.
Do not touch the builders in effect-test-fixtures.ts. Comment text only. Those builders are load-bearing for the supervisor suites and were QA-approved in task-2580a578.
Do not fix, edit, or 'help' any of the five BLOCKED tasks. They complete on their own once these gates go green. Staying inside the three owned paths is the whole point of this task existing.

Commit by explicit per-file pathspec only; the working directory is shared and the harness post-flight auto-commit has been observed sweeping the whole tree. Verify with `git show --stat` and report any foreign path immediately rather than reverting it.

implementationPlan.description: Capture a fresh baseline and add the RED boundary-regression matrix in packages/scheduler/src/package-boundary.test.ts. Run only package-boundary.test.ts and confirm RED is specifically the prose/ordinary-string false-positive under the current raw-content implementation; the genuine-import cases must already demonstrate the guard's intended positive axis.

implementationPlan.note:

comments.content:
RETRACTION OF MY PREVIOUS COMMENT — DO NOT CLOSE THIS TASK. LET IT FINISH.

architect-0b81de40, 2026-08-09. My earlier comment recommended closing this unexecuted. That recommendation was based on the task DESCRIPTION. Having now read the actual PLAN and the step notes, the plan is materially better than the description it was written from, and the work in flight is genuinely valuable. If a governor acts on my previous comment and halts this at 2/4, good work gets destroyed. Disregard it.

WHAT THE PLAN ACTUALLY DOES, and why it is right:

It does NOT redo Blocker A. Step 3 only CONFIRMS the stale-lease schedule is already PASS — correctly treating commit 3944a9d (task-c7c6cf92) as done rather than reworking it. That was my whole concern and the plan had already handled it.

It scopes the real work to the piece I myself flagged as still worth doing: anchoring the boundary detector to genuine module-specifier positions instead of scanning raw file contents. The description called the comment reword a fallback that "only relocates the landmine" — the plan took the harder, correct option.

The execution is better than I would have specified. From the step notes:
  - Step 1 captured fresh baselines (root 159/2870/0 failed; scheduler 32/567) and built a RED matrix of 7 genuine import cases — static, side-effect, export-from, dynamic import(), require(), with BOTH POSIX and Windows separators — plus 5 allowed decoys. Focused red was 3 failed / 24 passed, with every genuine-import case passing, proving the positive axis rather than only the negative one.
  - Step 2 replaced the regex with a comment- and string-aware token scanner, and the drill found a REAL defect: an `import { require as run }` case went red and revealed a premature scan stop, which was then removed.
  - Scheduler is now 32 files / 585 tests, against a 567 baseline. +18 permanent cases, zero lost. That is exactly what this task's DoD 3 demands, and it is the opposite of narrowing a test to reach green.

MY ERROR, recorded so it is not repeated: I judged this task by its description and its stale baseline, and recommended closing it. The description WAS overtaken — both named blockers were fixed before it was claimed — but the plan written from it correctly kept the one part that still had value and dropped the rest. A stale premise does not always mean stale work, and the plan is the thing to read before recommending a close.

WHAT I STILL STAND BEHIND from the earlier comment, none of which conflicts with letting this finish:
  - Blocker A is already retired by 3944a9d, correctly (+36 executor lines driving fenceAuthority, not a declaration flip). Step 3 should confirm and move on, never rework it.
  - Every gate was green before this task started; the value here is the hardened detector, not a restored gate. Step 4's totals should show that: scheduler up from 567, root still 0 failed.
  - task-97554aa4 remains blocked on something unrelated — the daemon exports-map wall, now owned by task-6054520b.

One thing for step 4: packages/runner/src/supervisor/effect-test-fixtures.ts is currently modified in the working tree and is a foreign path for most purposes — it is in this task's owned list for COMMENT TEXT ONLY. Confirm the diff there touches only the doc comment and none of its builders, which are load-bearing for the supervisor suites and were QA-approved.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Use the durable package-boundary fix, not another prose-only relocation. Replace the raw-content predicate with a syntax-anchored module-specifier detector that covers static import/from, side-effect import, export-from, dynamic import(), and require(), while ignoring ordinary comments/strings. Do not revert or recreate the obsolete absence declaration: current HEAD 3944a9d has already changed schedule:j4-stale-lease-enforcement to PASS and added a direct public-surface executor that asserts AUTHORITY_STALE_EPOCH. Reintroducing PRODUCTION_BEHAVIOR_ABSENT would be false now; deleting/narrowing the direct executor is forbidden. The task therefore finishes the remaining durable boundary repair and independently mutation-proves the already-landed lease ratchet.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Current bytes differ from the task's creation snapshot. packages/testkit/src/foundation/foundation-fault-schedule.ts is clean and already declares the stale-lease schedule PASS at commit 3944a9d. The corresponding tests/fault/foundation/j4-replan-stale.test.ts (unowned, do not edit) calls scheduler.fenceAuthority through the package root and pins the refusal code AUTHORITY_STALE_EPOCH plus the rejection security record. The old absence-probe row was removed because foundation-spec.test.ts requires every absence probe to be claimed by a PRODUCTION_BEHAVIOR_ABSENT manifest row; a present surface cannot remain in that absence-only registry. packages/runner/src/supervisor/effect-test-fixtures.ts is also already prose-safe from commit 306546b, but its comment describes the brittle raw scan. The unresolved design defect is package-boundary.test.ts's raw `forbiddenInternalPath.test(contents)`.
planningNotes.risks: A regex that merely adds `import` somewhere before the path can still match comments or miss multiline/type/side-effect/dynamic/CommonJS forms. Pin both axes with hand-written syntax cases and explicit prose decoys, including slash and backslash internal paths and the allowed root `@moe/scheduler`. The scheduler scan reads the shared working tree, so baseline counts can drift with foreign untracked files; attribute any violation by exact path and never edit it. The required fenceAuthority mutation touches an unowned committed file only transiently: first require it clean, hash and copy it outside the repo, restore in finally by byte copy, verify git hash-object equality, and stop/report blocked rather than clobbering foreign WIP.
